results.title: US House District 9: Will there be a recount? Osceola County set to submit election results for state to decide
results.summary:
Summary:
- In Florida’s newly redrawn US House District 9, incumbent Democrat Darren Soto leads Republican Dan Green by about 1,400 votes (0.52%) as of now.
- State law triggers a machine recount if the margin is 0.5% or less; the current 0.52% margin is just outside that threshold, so no automatic recount yet.
- Osceola County completed an audit; canvassing boards across the district will submit initial unofficial results to the state. The state will determine whether a recount is ordered after review.
- If margins shift with outstanding ballots, a recount could still be triggered. At this moment, the race appears not to meet recount criteria, but outcomes depend on pending results from seven counties comprising District 9 (Orange, Osceola, Polk, Indian River, Okeechobee, Highlands, Glades).
- The district’s status: Soto has declared victory, but results remain unofficial pending state determination.

Key takeaway for your query (state certification, recount, or court challenge): As of now, no automatic recount is triggered due to the 0.52% margin. Osceola County and other district counties must finalize and submit results to the state; the state will decide if a machine recount is required. Potential for a recount hinges on pending ballots and state review, not yet determined by a court challenge.

results.title: What's next for 10 close election contests in NC? | WUNC News
results.summary:
Summary:
- In North Carolina’s 2026 midterm contests, several close races could move to recounts or certifications after county canvasses on November 13. 
- Congressional races with potential recounts: Bobbing close leads in NC districts 7 (Rouzer), 3 (Murphy), and 5 (Foxx trailing Hubbard by 99 votes) could trigger recounts if margins stay under 1% of total votes.
- Statehouse significance: Six state House races and one state Senate race (Sen. Danny Britt, R-Robeson, leading by under 300) could decide party control of the Senate (Russian: Republicans 26 seats vs Democrats 24 if Britt’s lead holds).
- Process timing: Recounts can be requested once canvass meetings occur; provisional and mail-in ballots added in the days after Election Day can alter leads. Official results follow post-election canvassing and ballot curing processes.
- Certification path: Final results will be certified after canvassing and any required ballot curing, with potential changes to unofficial Election Night tallies. Unofficial results are not final until certification.

If you want, I can tailor this to focus on either congressional recount procedures, state Senate control implications, or the certification timeline and how to file a challenge.
